chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Fazala ibn Ayoub, from Al-Sakuni, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was gloomy and distressed, so he said to me: 'O Sakuni, from what is your gloom?' I said, 'A daughter has been born to me.' He said: 'O Sakuni, upon the earth is her weight (to carry), and upon Allah is her sustenance. She will live outside your lifespan and eat from other than your sustenance.' So, by Allah, he comforted me.

He said to me, 'What have you named her?' I said, 'Fatima.' He said, 'Aah! Aah!' Then he placed his hand on his forehead and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The right of a child upon its parent, if it is male, is that he respects his mother, approves of his name, teaches him the Book of Allah, purifies him, and teaches him swimming. And if it is female, he respects her mother, approves of her name, teaches her Surah Al-Nur, does not teach her Surah Yusuf, does not keep her in the chambers, and hastens her release to the house of her husband.'
As for if you name her Fatima, do not insult her, do not curse her, and do not hit her.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a father towards his daughter according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinct pedagogical and social strategies for raising daughters, specifically advising against teaching Surah Yusuf to mitigate the risks of beauty and marriageability, while emphasizing early marriage. The Imam’s specific instruction for the name 'Fatima'—to avoid cursing or striking her—reflects the unique status of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) as a model of purity and dignity in Shia tradition, linking the child's identity to her namesake's virtues.
